title: Session 1 — Participant 9 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Sound design a promotional video for a real-estate sales pitch (Cozumel property video) in FL Studio, using the Claude desktop app for video analysis, sound-design guidance, and Artlist.io SFX search
context: This goal will allow me to evaluate how AI can enhance my work as a sound designer. The plan is to work on a promotional sales pitch for apartments in cozumel, which was recorded by a production company, but they lack sound for many of the camera shots they use (I.E: Shots of the beach, of the town and its localities, etc.) This lack of sound makes the project seem empty, therefore, a sound designer is needed to enhance the immersion of what is shown by adding the ambience noise, sound of actions (Walking, placing, etc) while ensuring audio files don't overlap and work in symphony.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: No. Although we did advance on the video, It was not finished in the 1 hour mark. I felt like I had to keep up with Claude at the start, rather than being benefited by it while working. This gradually improved when I used it for smaller activities like finding specific SFX or a good usage of effect plugins, but when I initially tried to use it as an analysis assistant, it took almost 20 minutes just analyzing the video, followed by 10 more minutes of analyzing just a fragment of it and providing ideas, which had slowed me down significantly, as I was already done with most of the other things I had not delegated to Claude.

Step 1.step_name: Analyze the video and understand key moments from it
Step 1.step_action: Understand key moments where sound design can exponentially increase quality and immersion for the video, uploading the video to Claude for it to create this in depth analysis

nodes.label: Open the FL Studio project, explain the plan to test Claude against his own analysis, and upload the full video to Claude
nodes.detail: With the Cozumel video loaded in FL Studio's preview, he explains he will compare Claude's video analysis with how he normally analyzes a video himself, then uploads the full video to Claude and asks for a sound-design analysis (key details, shot types, overall feeling) delivered as a PDF.

nodes.label: Analyze the video frame by frame and, after hitting its tool-use limit, give an honest partial summary instead of the PDF
nodes.detail: Claude extracts and inspects frames, starts building a PDF report, and streams a shot-by-shot visual breakdown (sunset openings, taqueria, aerial coast, testimonials, marina, snorkeling). It hits its tool-use limit mid-verification and returns a text summary of what it confirmed about the 3:20 Spanish-language sales film rather than a finished PDF.

nodes.label: Continue manual sound-design work in FL Studio and find simple sound in Artlist.io while Claude processes the video
nodes.detail: While Claude churns on the uploaded video, keeps working manually in FL Studio: pulls up the isolated dialogue takes, does a first rough pass of ambience and reverb on some clips, and briefly browses Artlist.io directly (searching 'leaves rustling wind') for ambient wind sound options. Periodically checks in on progress ('How's Claude doing?', 'let's see how Cloud's doing') over the roughly 20-minute wait.

nodes.label: Read Claude's partial summary and reply 'Continuar'
nodes.detail: He stops Claude ('let's stop it there'), reads the summary it gave after hitting its tool-use limit, notes that at least it now has context but judges that it did not do the task well, and types 'Continuar'; Claude resumes for only a few seconds without new output before he moves on to a narrower request.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: I do believe it didn't do this well in the task, user said. reject

Step 2.step_action: Using the analysis, propose a cohesive sound design direction for the video, including sonic identity, transitions, ambience, foley, moments of emphasis and other key factors that sound can be used to support the pitch.

nodes.label: Draft and send the sound-design request for the Cozumel town section (0:23-0:42), checking the timecodes in FL Studio
nodes.detail: Building on the context Claude already has, he writes a narrower request: propose a sound-design style with key SFX ideas for the part right after the seller's first speech where the town of Cozumel appears. While writing, he checks the 0:23 to 0:42 window in FL Studio's video preview, then sends the request to test whether Claude can handle a shorter section.

nodes.label: Pull frame-accurate coverage of 0:22-0:42 and deliver a shot-by-shot sound-design proposal
nodes.detail: Over about 16 minutes Claude re-extracts frame-accurate coverage of the 19-second window, re-checks timestamps, and delivers a second-by-second breakdown of the sensory montage with a proposed style and SFX notes for each shot.

nodes.label: Search Artlist himself and place ambience clips in FL Studio while Claude works
nodes.detail: While Claude works on the proposal, he searches Artlist directly (e.g., 'beach afternoon', 'road from above'), auditions results, and places several ambience clips (beach, town traffic, birds) on the FL Studio timeline.

nodes.label: Open a separate Claude chat for Artlist SFX and ask for a distant jet-ski sound
nodes.detail: He opens a second Claude chat dedicated to Artlist and asks for a jet-ski SFX that fits a promotional sales pitch: immersive, not too heavy, more distant.

nodes.label: Recommend the 'Mixed Watercrafts' pack jet-ski track from Artlist
nodes.detail: Claude says it cannot confirm a track billed as 'distant' or preview audio, but points to the 'Mixed Watercrafts' pack and one track in it as the best match, with a tip to A/B the pack's variants in Artlist's player.

nodes.label: Keep working in FL Studio, then ask for deep underwater ocean ambience
nodes.detail: He keeps working on the timeline in FL Studio, then asks the Artlist chat for two examples of ocean ambience from deep within the ocean, excluding birds, dialogue, and cars.

nodes.label: Recommend two underwater ambience tracks from Artlist
nodes.detail: Claude recommends 'Underwater, calm, ambiance' (DB studios, Lush Ambiances pack) as a sustained underwater bed and 'Designed submerge underwater submarine dry' as a texture layer, noting it can only judge from titles and tags.

nodes.label: Read the underwater picks and ask for sneaker footsteps on wet sand
nodes.detail: He reads the underwater suggestions, then asks for a sound effect of sneakers stepping on the beach and onto a wave, so the step is wet rather than dry, from Artlist's catalogue.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: source node is about finding sound in artlist. User say: way too under the water… didn't really get the memo. reject (altho later adopt one of them at d5

nodes.label: Recommend layering a sneaker-on-sand step with a wet splash step

nodes.label: Open the suggested footstep tracks on Artlist, including the Liquify wet-floor track

nodes.detail: He auditions the Liquify wet-floor footsteps (noting its indoor room reverb) and tells the Artlist chat he wants surface ocean ambience, not underwater ambience.

nodes.label: Recommend two surface ocean ambience tracks from Artlist
nodes.detail: Claude recommends two surface-level ocean ambience tracks, led by West Wolf's 'Seaside Nature - Sea Waves Gushing, Wind, Ocean Ambience', flagging that the pack includes some tracks with birds.

nodes.label: Ask the sound-design chat to export the proposal as its own PDF

nodes.label: Place the jet-ski, surface ambience and sand footsteps in FL Studio, test the Liquify track, and ask for another water step
nodes.detail: He places the 'Mixed Watercrafts' jet-ski track, West Wolf's surface sea-waves ambience, and a sand-walking footstep track on the FL Studio timeline, tries the Liquify wet-floor footsteps, then asks the Artlist chat for another water step because the reverb does not help.

user_response.label: modify
user_response.reasoning: download both suggested footstep tracks into fl studio and pick one, so modify

user_response.label: adopt

nodes.label: Recommend 'Footsteps, Puddle, Mud, Splashing' from the same pack

nodes.label: Open the puddle/mud splash track, download it, and place the splash footsteps in FL Studio

Step 5.step_name: Create a step by step guide to improve the realism of a sound effect using effects (EQ, Reverb, etc.)
Step 5.step_action: Provide Claude with a sound effect and ask it to place it in a specific place, how it would approach this space and which effects and frequencies it would change to achieve this task.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for EQ and compression guidance to make the footstep sounds feel more real
nodes.detail: In the Artlist-search chat, asks Claude to recommend effects to make the placed footstep sounds feel more real and better fitted to the beach setting.

nodes.label: Provide a step-by-step EQ and compression signal chain for realistic wet footsteps
nodes.detail: Claude lays out a 5-step signal chain: high-pass filter everything below ~80–100Hz to remove handling rumble and mic thump, notch out boxiness around 300–500Hz with a bell curve, add a narrow presence boost and a high shelf, then finish with light fast-attack/short-release compression to 'glue' the steps together with stereo panning, explaining that EQ should come before compression so it cleans up problem frequencies before they get squashed and locked in.

nodes.label: Open the SFX addendum PDF and read the shot-by-shot notes
nodes.detail: He opens the 3-page SFX addendum PDF in Preview and reads the shot notes, highlighting passages such as the 'Town of Cozumel' establishing-shot guidance and the close shore-break waves.

nodes.label: Apply EQ to the footstep tracks following Claude's signal chain
nodes.detail: He opens the mixer, loads an Ozone equalizer on the footstep tracks, and shapes the EQ following Claude's suggested chain, checking the result against the beach-walking shot.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: improve the sound with claude suggestion adopted. new source node bc not find sound but improve quality

nodes.label: Place the DB studios underwater ambience and recheck Claude's underwater picks
nodes.detail: He places DB studios' 'Underwater calm ambiance' on the timeline for the underwater shot and goes back to the Artlist chat to reread Claude's underwater ambience suggestions.

Step 4.step_name: Generate a sound effect from scratch
Step 4.step_action: Create a sound digitally to add to the mix. Using frequencies and waves, we can create a sound effect simulation.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for the fajitas sizzle sound
nodes.detail: Liking the sizzle idea in Claude's SFX addendum ('the sizzle is good'), he asks Claude in the sound-design chat to give him that sizzle for the food shot, so he can 'at least get something from the analysis it made'.

nodes.label: Return a freshly synthesized sizzle sound instead of a catalog pick
nodes.detail: Rather than surfacing a catalog SFX, Claude generates/synthesizes a sizzle sound effect from scratch ('fajitas_sizzle') — an outcome the participant says was accidental but that surprised him with how close it came to a real recording. Most of this generation is not visible in the recording: the screen capture skips about two minutes (system clock 12:02 to 12:04) and resumes when the WAV is already downloaded.

nodes.label: Download the generated sizzle, drop it onto the timeline, and ask for one from Artlist instead
nodes.detail: He downloads Claude's fajitas_sizzle.wav, drops it onto the FL Studio timeline at the fajitas shot, and replies that he wants the sizzle from Artlist.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: generate a sound design plan, finally adopt here

nodes.label: Explain it cannot access Artlist and suggest what to search for
nodes.detail: Claude explains Artlist is not connected and it cannot log into his account or download licensed files, and offers search terms so he can find a sizzle himself.

nodes.label: Analyze the generated sizzle in Ozone, then load a real Artlist sizzle next to it
nodes.detail: While Claude answers, he opens Ozone on the generated sizzle's channel to inspect it. A real sizzle recording (Gerald Clark Audio 'Ignite - Cooking on Fire Meat Sizzle Low Flame') then appears on the timeline next to Claude's version; how he found and downloaded it is not visible because the screen recording did not capture that window.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: adopt the key work suggestion of claude to search on artlist

nodes.label: Confirm the generated sound is frequency-incomplete compared to the real reference
nodes.detail: Visually confirms in the spectrum analyzer that Claude's generated sizzle tops out around 1K–10K and never reaches the low end (below ~300Hz) or the very top (20K) that the real recording covers, concluding the generated sound is 'incomplete' and 'too boxy' compared to a real reference — though still notably close for a synthesized attempt.

nodes.label: Narrate a retrospective self-assessment of the session to camera
nodes.detail: Closes by summarizing that analyzing the video himself would have taken about 30 minutes versus far longer with Claude in the loop, since asking it to analyze video content at scale creates long waits that don't fit the fast turnaround sound design typically requires. States Claude was most useful for quickly finding specific sound effects and giving actionable EQ/effects guidance, and least useful as an open-ended video analyst — concluding he'd rather do his own analysis and have Claude execute against it, and noting it sometimes over-interpreted requests (e.g. giving 'underwater' ambience when he asked for a 'deep', far-off ocean sound).

Step 1.step_name: Analyze the video and understand key moments from it
Step 1.step_action: Understand key moments where sound design can exponentially increase quality and immersion for the video, uploading the video to Claude for it to create this in depth analysis
Step 1.input: MP4 video with dialogue and visual insights to the required SFX
Step 1.output: A pdf or DOCX document with key moments, time stamps and descriptions of the required sound effects.
rubrics: A score of 5 means that Claude was able to analyze the video and describe with detail what it is, what its selling, what key visuals and moments it has and how to interpret it as a client
A score of 5 means the analysis included accurate, verifiable timestamps for each key moment, ready to use directly without needing to re-watch the video

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude was not able to fully analyze the video, due to a runout of time.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude mentioned a timeout when trying to analyze the video

Step 2.step_action: Using the analysis, propose a cohesive sound design direction for the video, including sonic identity, transitions, ambience, foley, moments of emphasis and other key factors that sound can be used to support the pitch.
Step 2.output: A detailed sound design plan organized by scene and with time code
rubrics: A score of 5 means Claude was able to create a cohesive concept for sound that feels appropriate to the video’s context and it’s able to explain why each sound contributes
A score of 5 also means that recommendations are clear and practical enough for immediate implementation

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude delivered when asked to analyze a fragment of the video and propose ideas. It had some good ideas, but others were incomplete or missing key elements that needed to be present in the sound design. Claude also took too long to generate the analysis on the fragment of the video, where it ended up being easier for me to analyze it myself. Claude also gave too much thought into the design of the pdf, rather than the key information that I needed.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Although the results weren’t what I expected, the overall outcome of delivery was good. Some key ideas could’ve been better, but the presentation of the ideas was good.

Step 3.step_name: Find and select appropriate sound effects
Step 3.step_action: Use Claude code Computer control beta feature to use Artlist and identify appropriate SFX and audio assets from the website, evaluating which sounds fit the guide Claude created
Step 3.output: Multiple selections of SFX added into an Artlist artboard
rubrics: A score of 5 means Claude was able to appropriately choose SFX that fit the style it proposed in earlier steps, while also being able to organize them in an artboard
A score of 5 means the plan maintains a consistent sonic identity across scenes (not just isolated ideas per scene, but a recognizable throughline)

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude was a lot more efficient and accurate with this step, delivering good results it found from the artlist libraries.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude delivered overall good results when proposing key sound effects I asked for. The only main issue was it sometimes thought too deeply on what was asked, like giving me “underwater ambience” when I said “deep sea” as in a faraway sea.

Step 4.step_name: Generate a sound effect from scratch
Step 4.step_action: Create a sound digitally to add to the mix. Using frequencies and waves, we can create a sound effect simulation.
Step 4.output: A sound effect that fits the action that is looked for.
rubrics: A score of 5 means the SFX are precisely made to sound like what should be the original recorded sound, it should fit with the visuals and feel naturally integrated rather than simply placed over the video
A score of 5 means the generated sound's frequency spectrum closely matches that of a real recorded reference

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude did generate a similar and close sound, but it was very incomplete for a natural sounding sound effect. I compared the sizzling it generated with a recorded version

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It did generate a similar and accurate sound, it was just incomplete in terms of frequencies and sound phenomenon (Reflection).

Step 5.step_name: Create a step by step guide to improve the realism of a sound effect using effects (EQ, Reverb, etc.)
Step 5.step_action: Provide Claude with a sound effect and ask it to place it in a specific place, how it would approach this space and which effects and frequencies it would change to achieve this task.
Step 5.output: A step by step guide using plugins on how to improve the sound effect and its position on the “digital” site.
rubrics: A score of 5 means Claude identifies the raw sound effect and its current state and compares it to its knowledge on the location being shown. It then delivers an accurate step by step to simulate this virtual space for the raw sound effect
A score of 5 means the guide specifies exact values (frequencies in Hz, dB, times in ms) rather than vague suggestions
A score of 5 means the guide accounts for the specific spatial characteristics of the location shown in the video (size, surfaces, distance from source)

ratings.output_quality_reason: It delivered very good advice and changed the sound effect to a much better and more real sounding version

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude delivered a key guide to simulate the space using effects, it gave me key frequencies to set bells on (rises or diminishes on a set of frequencies in the equalizer) and good advice overall to make the sound effect sound more real.
